speaker: Pete Hegseth
venue: Signed C-UAS guidance (announced by JIATF-401, Jan 2026)
quote: Countering drones does not start and stop at the fence line (BG Ross, describing the guidance)
points: Consolidates Title 10 / 10 U.S.C. 130i C-UAS policy; commanders can act beyond installation fence lines with coordination.
Unauthorized drone surveillance of designated facilities is now explicitly a threat, so engagement is allowed before a perimeter breach.
Service secretaries can designate which facilities are 'covered'.
Allows active and passive sensing and electromagnetic defeat; commanders must coordinate with the FAA.
Guillot: the military sees 1-2 incursions per day.
um_relevance: More covered facilities plus engagement outside the fence means more sites need a mobile, forward effector. A pursuing interceptor that carries its own sensors suits defense beyond the perimeter.

speaker: DoD Office of Inspector General
quote: DOD officials told us that training is not covered. Therefore, installation officials cannot use C-UAS capabilities to prevent unmanned aerial system activity.
points: Major US installations lack C-UAS despite policy mandates; 20+ conflicting DoD C-UAS policies.
Luke AFB (trains 75% of the world's F-35 pilots), Air Force Plant 42, and SUPSHIP Newport News flagged as uncovered or ambiguous.
Recommends JIATF-401 consolidate policy, roles, covered-facility requirements and the 130i approval process.
um_relevance: Documented coverage gaps at high-value sites create near-term demand; procurement follows once facilities are designated.

speaker: Congressional Budget Office
venue: Report: Options to Counter Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems
quote: No single system would provide full protection (paraphrase of CBO's layered-defense conclusion)
points: ~$74M to equip one representative installation with layered defense, plus ~$5M/yr to support it.
Protecting 100 bases: up to $7.4B upfront plus ~$500M/yr; DoD tracks 824 installations.
Defeat methods listed: entangling, impeding communications, or destroying with projectiles or directed energy.
Systems may need full replacement every 4-5 years; 135 vendors answered DoD demo requests.
um_relevance: CBO names entanglement as a defeat category alongside kinetic and DE. A $74M per-base layered architecture leaves room for a low-cost, reusable capture interceptor layer.

speaker: Dan Driscoll
quote: They're about $15,000 a piece right now. We think as they scale, they'll get less than [$10,000]
points: 10,000 Merops interceptors shipped to the Middle East within five days of the Feb 28, 2026 strikes on Iran.
Acquisition decision cut from a '16-step' process to an immediate group decision.
With larger orders, interceptors could fall to $3,000-5,000 each (Bloomberg).
um_relevance: The price target for interceptor drones is now set publicly at $3-10K. UM's airframe ($25K placeholder) only wins on cost if recovery and reuse are proven — this is the benchmark investors will use.

speaker: Markwayne Mullin; Kash Patel; Troy Edgar
role: DHS Secretary; FBI Director; DHS Deputy Secretary
venue: House Appropriations Homeland Security Subcommittee, FY27 budget
quote: We have more people asking to get into the school than he has space
points: 300+ drones taken down across World Cup venues; 50+ seized in Dallas; 60 systems seized and 52 operators ticketed around Miami.
Only 8 of 22 DHS components run C-UAS, with differing approaches; DHS weighing a joint C-UAS task force.
The FBI National Counter-UAS Training Center (Huntsville) is the throughput bottleneck for SLTT certification.
um_relevance: Homeland demand is real and operational; training and certification capacity, not hardware, is the pacing item for state and local mitigation.

speaker: Kash Patel
quote: (FBI) prevented an attack targeting UFC Freedom 250 (paraphrase)
points: Alleged plot: explosive-armed drones to panic the crowd, then snipers, then a second wave on the White House, at the June 14, 2026 South Lawn event.
5+ arrests across 12 FBI field offices (OH, MO, CA).
um_relevance: A domestic armed-drone plot against a mass gathering is the threat case for a capture effector cleared for populated areas.

speaker: Pete Hegseth
quote: We're moving fast — cutting through bureaucracy, consolidating resources, and empowering this task force with the utmost authority to outpace our adversaries
points: JIATF-401 replaced the Joint Counter-small UAS Office (JCO), stood up by Army Secretary Driscoll, with a 36-month initial mandate.
May approve up to $50M per initiative to accelerate C-UAS fielding.
um_relevance: One accountable buyer now exists for C-sUAS, with its own money ($1.4B in the House FY27 bill) — UM's primary target customer.

speaker: Maj. Mike Hapner
quote: the right counter-UAS capabilities to the right users at the right time
points: Public C-UAS Marketplace at cuas.mil launched Aug 2026 (IOC Feb 24-25, 2026; 1,600+ items by March).
Built by Kaizen Labs under a $15M OTA (May 2026).
Vendors apply and pass vetting — business verification, export-control review, product evaluation — before listing.
Buyers: services, COCOMs, federal interagency (DHS/DOJ/FBI), and pre-cleared allied MoDs. Australia bought off drones.mil about 10 days before Sept 24.
um_relevance: The marketplace is the cheapest route to federal buyers for a startup. UM should start vendor vetting as soon as it has test data.

speaker: Dan Driscoll
venue: Low-Cost Interceptor Industry Day, Crystal City
quote: We're not going to do this physical process where we are whiteboarding deep in the Pentagon
points: LCI target <$250K per interceptor, but 'if somebody came in with 280,000 [or] 420,000... we're going to buy it'.
Component white papers due July 6; 120-day development clock; live fire at White Sands in fall 2026.
Open architecture, government data and IP sharing among component providers.
um_relevance: LCI is sized for Shahed-class jets and cruise missiles; UM's lower-cost Group 1-2 niche is underneath it. Watch for a Group 1-2 interceptor variant or component calls.
